text:
alicia: Heads up — noticed a cluster of tiny requests on the cost dashboard with huge per-token charges. Looks like billing and cache signals disagree. anyone seen this pattern?

mike: saw spikes on the canary dashboard earlier. small prompt sizes but billed tokens look inflated. seems correlated to recent router namespace change.

sandeep: could be attribution change for shared prefetch. we moved from a shared-credit model to route-level crediting last sprint.

judy: can you paste an example invocation id so we can trace?

alicia: inv-2024-11-05-a7c. console excerpt: 
```
token_count=8
billed_units=24
cache_prefetch_credits=0
cache_key_namespace=ns_v1
model=redwood-7b-q4
```

mike: interesting. router recently started appending tenant suffix to cache keys (ns_v2). if writers still use ns_v1 we get misses. billing then counts full decode cost and we attempt a prefetch that never credits.

zach: that tenant-suffix change was to avoid cross-tenant collisions. might not have completed key churn for long-lived caches.

ops-bot: fetched sample log for inv-2024-11-05-a7c:
- route: /v1/generate
- model: redwood-7b-q4
- cache_key_seen: device:42:hash:abcd (namespace ns_v1)
- router_variant: suffix-tenants (reads ns_v2)
- prefetch_events: attempted=1, success=0

sandeep: confirmation: mismatch between writer key and reader key. we don't currently surface cache_key_version or prefetch outcome in the console cost card which makes debugging painful.

alicia: proposal: add a lightweight "cost inspector" mode on the invocation details panel. When enabled (sampled) it shows: hashed_cache_key, cache_namespace_version, prefetch_attempts, prefetch_success, billed_tokens, model_sku. Default off.

mike: agree but telemetry budget worries. these fields should be sent only for sampled invocations. default sampling 0.05% org-wide, and a tenant-level override for enterprise accounts.

judy: privacy check: do not show any raw prompt text in inspector. only expose prompt_hash and short metadata. add audit logging for those who view inspector.

sandeep: implementation thought: expose an internal admin endpoint /internal/debug/cost?invocation_id=<id>&sample=true that returns minimal JSON text fields (invocation_id, billed_tokens, cache_namespace, prefetch_attempts, prefetch_success, model) and requires X-Internal-Debug header. console calls this when user expands inspector UI.

zach: debate: should services emit a fire-and-forget envelope to telemetry (topic: cost-inspector) at request end, or should console request the debug payload on demand?

mike: push model pros: realtime, simple UX for on-call, but adds writes to telemetry path. poll model pros: fewer events by default, simpler retention, but slower and adds load when many operators query. my vote: hybrid — router emits compact cache event for every invocation to a low-cost topic with strict sampling; console can do on-demand call to billing service for join data when user asks for full view.

alicia: UX: show a small "inspector" pill next to cost amount when sampled trace exists. clicking expands an inline pane with the minimal fields and a link "view full trace" that opens the infra-only debug console.

judy: rollout checklist idea: 1) backend: emit compact cache events (schema below) behind flag; 2) console: add inspector UI behind feature flag; 3) enable sampling 0.05% org-wide; 4) enterprise override via tenant settings; 5) monitor telemetry topic traffic for 72h; 6) legal review of exposure policy.

sandeep: suggested compact Kafka envelope (single-line JSON string in event body):
```
{ "invocation_id": "inv-2024-11-05-a7c", "model": "redwood-7b-q4", "billed_tokens": "24", "cache_namespace": "ns_v1", "prefetch_attempts": "1", "prefetch_success": "0" }
```

mike: billing join must remain single source of truth. router should not compute final cost. emit event refs only; billing service performs join and writes billed tokens. console should display billing payload and any sampled cache events joined by invocation_id.

zach: added a quick SQL to help ops reconcile suspicious cases: 
```
SELECT v.invocation_id, v.billed_tokens, e.cache_namespace, e.prefetch_success, e.prefetch_attempts
FROM billing.invocations v
LEFT JOIN telemetry.compact_cache_events e ON v.invocation_id = e.invocation_id
WHERE v.billed_tokens > 10 AND v.invocation_ts > now() - interval '7 days'
ORDER BY v.billed_tokens DESC
LIMIT 100;
```

judy: I'll add the SQL to the runbook and annotate common root causes (namespace drift, key churn, model sku fallback).

sandeep: I'll prototype the event emitter and the internal endpoint. will ensure the payload is tiny and gzipped.

alicia: i'll draft a short RFC covering schema, sampling, console changes, privacy constraints, and ops runbook. schedule a quick review with legal and infra. target: ship canary in 2 weeks.

mike: one more note — add rate caps so a tenant can't accidentally enable 100% debug and flood telemetry. cap default tenant override at 1% unless infra-approved.

zach: ack. I'll prepare key-migration plan to rotate namespaces with a shadow reader mode for 48h to catch mismatches.

alicia: great. Thanks everyone. we'll reconvene next Tue to review the RFC + prototype. :rocket:
